partner_result_applied.statement_used: For the fully rotated three-bank uniform witness, p_Qm(0)=3sqrt(2)[1-5295/(21952m)+O(m^-2)] with a polynomially weighted local Edgeworth remainder.

new_mathematics.statement: For the partner fully rotated witness, replace each physical coordinate law by f_m=(1-c/m^2)1_[-1/2,1/2]+1_{R_m}, where R_m has total length c/m^2 and is centered at +/-a sqrt(m). Then p_Qm(0)/(3sqrt(2))=1-5295/(21952m)+(c/m)sum_j(R_j(a)-1)+o(m^-1), where every R_j(a)<= (1+exp(-6a^2))/2. Hence limsup m[p_Qm(0)/(3sqrt(2))-1] <= -5295/21952-(3c/2)(1-exp(-6a^2))<0.
new_mathematics.core_lemma: For G~N(h,vI_3), S_h=G1^2+G2^2-G3^2 obeys p_Sh(0)/p_S0(0)<= (1+exp(-||h||^2/(2v)))/2. The proof Poisson-expands noncentral chi-squares and uses r_00=1, sup_nonzero r_kl=1/2.
new_mathematics.target_implication: Vanishing-intensity m^-2 mesoscopic remote fragments at distance Theta(sqrt(m)) cannot improve the 3sqrt(2) sharp witness; they strictly worsen the first-order deficit. A stronger lower-bound witness must leave the isolated noncentral-Gaussian mean-shift perturbative regime.

unresolved_implication: This does not treat order-1/m fragment mass with a nontrivial compound-Poisson limit in a shared-coordinate frame, growing/nonperiodic frames, multiscale fragment populations, arbitrary finite leverage, or arbitrary extra spectrum.
next_step: Change mechanism to order-1/m fragmented shared-coordinate rotated frames or multiscale fragments; seek either a peak above 3sqrt(2) or a product-preserving barrier beyond convex mixtures of noncentral Gaussian cone-tip profiles.
